outcome: Mirror every live workflow in a predictive simulation updated from telemetry

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Execution Digital Twin Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Execution Digital Twin Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, state snapshots, predictions, and scenario branches required to mirror every live workflow in a predictive simulation updated from telemetry, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for intent compilation, execution graphs, routing, reversibility, recovery, and long-running autonomous operations; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Execution Digital Twin Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: mirror every live workflow in a predictive simulation updated from telemetry.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Execution Digital Twin Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Execution Digital Twin Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using causal planning, speculative execution, constraint optimization, digital twins, and anomaly detection.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Execution Digital Twin Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the execution map, route debugger, scenario sandbox, and autonomous operations console, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Execution Digital Twin into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Execution Digital Twin Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Execution Digital Twin Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: The system sees likely bottlenecks and failures before they happen. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
